diagrams.reason: All report sections and five infographic panels were assessed, plus seven additional mechanisms. No candidate survives the non-duplication and relationship tests. S1 (Where does a note live before the Event Task exists?): Duplicates the report's existing private-note data-flow Mermaid figure. S2 (Which event classes benefit from private notes?): The three event classes and their present-day failures are already fully compared in a table. S3 (What does Bob control, and what does Google retain?): The requirement-adjustment table already states all of these ownership boundaries. S4 (Why choose layering over pre-touching or seeding once?): The verdict table already compares every alternative; arrows would invent a decision procedure. S5 (Which source wins for each field?): The precedence table already gives every field's ordered layers and reason/prose rules. S6 (How does sync respond to missing or corrupt notes?): The reliability table already states the corruption guard's full conjunction and response; do not turn it into a diagram. S7 (Why prefer a vault note over the alternatives?): The options table already states verdicts and reasons, with no additional dependency structure. S8 (What must ship before the feature is complete?): The phase table already gives the delivery order and work; a chart would be a short linear chain. S9 (How would phone-first RSVPing change the plan?): One conditional sentence answers it: frequent phone RSVPs move the Keep path earlier. S10 (How does saved intent become an Event Task?): Duplicates the report's existing data-flow Mermaid figure. S11 (Which evidence supports the recommendation?): This is a source list, not a stated evidence-dependency mechanism; arrows would add unsupported relationships. P1 (Why attach the note to the event before its task exists?): The existing data-flow figure and When a note lands table already show the timing relationship. P2 (How do before and after buffers change occupied time?): The prose gives the before/after rule in one sentence, and the console example supplies the exact occupied span. P3 (How does a private note combine with Google's fields?): The precedence table already expresses the complete field-by-field combination. P4 (What happens to a note after a reschedule, reset, or recreation?): The reliability table already gives each reschedule, reset, and recreation outcome. P5 (What ships now, next, and optionally for phones?): The implementation table and phone list already supply all phases and conditions. M1 (How does CLI text become canonical directive and reason lines?): The numbered normalization rules and examples already include every parsing branch this figure would draw. M2 (How are ambiguous event queries and unverified URLs handled?): The Selecting the event list item already supplies exact-ID validation, search fallback, and TTY/non-TTY branches. M3 (Why can a saved buffer update fail to reach an existing row?): One sentence already answers the question: a changed note applies only while the whole row is untouched. M4 (Which side parses input, previews, and writes the vault?): One paragraph directly assigns parsing, candidates, preview, and saving to bob; an exchange diagram would invent ordering. M5 (What happens when a phone note does not resolve uniquely?): The phone list already states both unique-match and ordinary-inbox fallback paths. M6 (How do concurrent host edits choose one saved note?): The fold list item already gives the full ordering tuple and append/clear rule; no further mechanism is stated. M7 (What remains active when description bullets are disabled?): One sentence answers it: bullets are hidden while directives still apply.
